{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I was assigned the bottom body line (stroke 3), and it was the slowest piece. At 2:15 I was under halfway, and the line stalled well short of the tail for a while. Sofia had to lay the back half from the tail to close it, so I can't claim the full stroke as mine. Once it was closed, the bottom line fell end to end into the tail. I also inspected the fins around 6:45 and flagged the break at the start of the upper fin and the jammed spot past the junction. Sofia and Hana then fixed both. I haven't seen the push result, so I can't say yet whether the judge will recognise the fish. The design itself (nose split, body, forked tail) should read clearly.

**Execution:** This is my weakest area. My pace was behind what the table needed, and my 'about a dozen from done' estimate at 3:30 was optimistic. I did communicate honestly when I was behind. I stayed hands-off in the final stretch, which avoided bumps near the junction. I did not catch the start-to-nose gap. Hana found it, and it could have stopped almost everything from falling.

**Collaboration:** I accepted Sofia's offer to meet me in the middle straight away, and I kept the table updated on my progress. I used my inspection to give Hana and Jack specific, useful info rather than just cheering. I also kept the mood light and confirmed hands-off before the push. I could have asked for help earlier instead of waiting until the bottom line was clearly behind.

**Leadership:** I didn't lead this one. Hana drove the plan and the checks, and Sofia handled the integration. My contribution was morale and a clear status when asked. Next time I would flag a slipping stroke sooner and offer to pick up someone else's piece when mine is the bottleneck, rather than relying on others to rescue it."}
